definitions.explanation: Items offered to deities, spirits of the deceased, or at Buddhist altars. Typically includes food, drink, flowers, and other items placed at shrines, temples, graves, or household altars.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いた→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: I placed an offering on the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧とお⟦{菓子|かし}→菓子：00191_kashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}した→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧。
examples.english: I prepared fruit and sweets as offerings.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{神棚|かみだな}→神棚：13740_kamidana⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{無事|ぶじ}→無事：01602_buji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祈|いの}る→祈る：01198_inoru⟧。
examples.english: At New Year's, we place offerings on the household shrine and pray for a safe year ahead.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
お{供|そな}え{物|もの} is central to Japanese religious practice. Common offerings include ⟦{米|こめ}→米：01323_kome⟧ (rice), ⟦{酒|さけ}→酒：02211_sake⟧ (sake), ⟦{果物|くだもの}→果物：00509_kudamono⟧ (fruit), ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧ (sweets), and ⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧ (flowers). After the offering period, food items are often consumed by the family, a practice called お{下|さ}がり.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to make an offering)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧ (to offer up)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧ (to take down an offering)

FORMS:
The plain form ⟦{供|そな}え{物|もの}→供え物：18160_sonaemono⟧ (without お) also exists but is less common in everyday speech.
